name: ASAP5
description: Optimized for detecting subthreshold activity, with the steepest F-V slope near resting potential.

spectrum.name: ASAP5
spectrum.note: Excitation digitized from Fig. 1a of the ASAP7y paper (Hao 2026). Emission is the shared cpGFP-family profile — ASAP5 emission is not reported in this figure.

voltage.name: ASAP5
voltage.note: Re-digitized 2026-09-08 from the Fig. 1D source crop (cyan ASAP5 curve, n = 5 HEK293A cells). Axis calibration from the printed x-ticks (-120/-70/-20/30/80 mV at x = 283/373/463/551/641 px) and y-ticks (60% to -80% at 69.4 px per 20%), cross-checked against the grey physiological band, which spans exactly -70 to +30 mV. Marker centres were located by erosion + connected components and overlay-verified. The eleven plotted voltage steps are -120, -100, -80, -70, -60, -40, -20, 0, +30, +50, +80 mV. The previous stored array mislabelled three of them (-60/-40/-20 were stored as -50/-30/-10), carried a +10 mV point that has no marker in the figure, and read -100 mV as +42% instead of +38%. The -70 to +30 mV step of -57% matches Table S2 (-57 +/- 2% at 23 C) exactly, and the +80 mV plateau of -60% matches the text.

kinetics.note: Bi-exponential fits at 37°C (Table S2). Activation: τ-fast 0.8 ms (95%), τ-slow 44.2 ms (5%) → amplitude-weighted mean 2.97 ms. Deactivation: τ-fast 1.1 ms (63%), τ-slow 5.2 ms (37%) → amplitude-weighted mean 2.62 ms. The paper headlines the fast components (0.78/1.12 ms).

Bi-exponential fits at 23°C (Table S2). Activation: τ-fast 2.6 ms (92%), τ-slow 45.3 ms (8%) → amplitude-weighted mean 6.02 ms. Deactivation: τ-fast 4.3 ms (75%), τ-slow 55.9 ms (25%) → amplitude-weighted mean 17.2 ms. The paper headlines the fast components (2.61/4.30 ms).

dynamicRangeData.note: Steady-state -ΔF/F for a -70 to +30 mV (100-mV) depolarizing step in HEK293A cells under one-photon widefield voltage clamp; -57 ± 2% at 23°C and -57 ± 3% at 37°C (Table S2). The F-V curve continues to a ~-60% plateau by +80 mV over the wider -70 to +80 mV sweep.
Response to a 100-mV depolarizing step from -70 mV at 33°C in HEK293A cells under 2P resonant scanning at 940 nm (Ext. Fig. 1b, n = 7 cells). Reduced response relative to JEDI-2P (41.8%) under 2P.

apWidthData.sample: Mouse, visual cortex L2/3 pyramidal neurons, awake behaving, in vivo, soma-targeted ASAP5-Kv (ULoVE 2P)
apWidthData.note: Optical action-potential waveform width (full width at half maximum) of the rapid post-threshold optical spike, recorded by ULoVE random-access 2P microscopy (920 nm) at 7142.9 Hz (two patterns/cell) in layer-2/3 visual cortex pyramidal neurons of awake behaving mice. Main text: 'FWHM of the rapid optical spike varies from sub-millisecond to 2 ms.' Bar (mean) digitized from the Fig. S4E 'Spike FWHM' panel ≈1.3 ms; the 11 per-neuron dots span 0.69-2.15 ms (mean of dots 1.32 ms), n = 11. Mammalian in-vivo cortex (~37°C; exact recording temperature not stated numerically). Axis-tick calibration ±~0.05 ms.

apWidthData.sample: Rat, cultured cortical neurons, current-evoked APs, in vitro

review.comment: Same issue with the FWHM of ASAP7, it's hard to believe that ASAP5 is narrower than ASAP7

apWidthData.note: Cross-GEVI entry from the ASAP7y paper (primary subject ASAP7y). Optical single-AP FWHM digitized from the averaged optical AP waveform in Fig. 1c (the cyan ΔF/F trace — average of n=7 cultured cortical neurons, plotted below the averaged electrical AP), calibrated to the panel's 20 ms scale bar and overlay-verified ≈ 6.8 ms (vs ASAP7y ≈ 10.3 ms in the same panel). This is a DIFFERENT regime from the Neuron-2024 ULoVE entry above (in-vivo 2P rapid post-threshold optical spike, 1.3 ms): here it is the slower full averaged optical AP waveform in culture. CAVEATS: the paper does not report this experiment's frame rate (samplingRate omitted), modality, or temperature for this panel; the ≈7 ms width is kinetics-dominated, not frame-rate-limited. RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-08 against the reviewer flag ('hard to believe that ASAP5 is narrower than ASAP7'): the panel was re-rendered at 600 dpi and re-measured independently (20 ms scale bar = 158 px; baseline from the flat pre-spike segment, peak from the max deflection) giving FWHM = 6.6 ms, confirming the stored 6.8 ms to within ±0.2 ms. The co-plotted averaged ELECTRICAL AP in the same panel measures ≈3.6 ms FWHM by the same method, so the optical waveform is ~1.8× broader than the voltage it reports. ASAP5 being narrower than ASAP7y here is the EXPECTED direction, not an error: ASAP7y's deactivation time constant is ~10.7 ms at 25 °C versus ASAP5's 4.3 ms (75% fast component, Table S2 of the Neuron 2024 paper), so the slower sensor smears the optical AP more. Both numbers are optical-waveform widths broadened by sensor kinetics and are not action-potential durations.

sensitivityData.note: Mean peak -ΔF/F per current-evoked action potential in cultured rat hippocampal neurons at room temperature, recorded by camera at 800 fps under one-photon widefield illumination (Fig. 1F, n = 10 cells). ~2-fold larger than ASAP3 (~17%).
Peak -ΔF/F per action potential in Drosophila TPN-II neurons in vivo under 940-nm two-photon excitation; ASAP7y responded 81% more strongly in the same prep

brightnessData.note: Per-neuron relative brightness in primary rat cortical neurons (Kv2.1-tagged constructs), normalized to ASAP4e-Kv = 1.0

photostabilityData.note: Effective irradiance ~20 mW/mm² (=46/2.3): Fig. S5E is an SNR-matched comparison vs Voltron2525-Kv — ASAP5-Kv was imaged at 46 mW/mm² but its time-axis was multiplied by 2.3 to plot the curve at the irradiance that yields the same SNR as Voltron2525-Kv at 46 mW/mm² (STAR Methods), so the plotted curve represents ~20 mW/mm². ~83% remaining at 1 min, digitized from the cyan ASAP5-Kv curve (full curve in photobleach[] below). CAVEAT: curves were normalized to the value at 0.5 s (the transient bright state in the first 0.5 s is excluded), so this slightly underestimates true bleaching; the cross-GEVI displayPhotostab normalization to 100 mW/mm² assumes linear photobleaching dose, which is consistent with the paper's own ×2.3 time-axis rescaling but should be read as approximate for this non-standard measurement.

photobleach.note: Digitized (cyan ASAP5-Kv curve) from Fig. S5E, the photostability comparison vs Voltron2525-Kv during mEPSP recordings in cultured rat neurons. RE-SCALED TO REAL ACQUISITION TIME (2026-09-08, per reviewer request): both sensors were actually imaged at 46 mW/mm² (STAR Methods), but the paper multiplied ASAP5-Kv's plotted time-axis by 2.3 to display an SNR-matched comparison at an effective ~20 mW/mm². Dividing the plotted time by 2.3 restores real seconds at 46 mW/mm², so this curve and the co-plotted Voltron2525-Kv curve (also 46 mW/mm²) are now an iso-irradiance comparison — which shows ASAP5-Kv bleaching FASTER than Voltron2525-Kv at equal power (0.83 vs 0.91 at 26 s); the paper's point is that ASAP5-Kv reaches the same mEPSP SNR at 2.3-fold lower power. The digitized fluorescence values were independently re-verified against the figure (max deviation 0.003). Normalized to the 0.5 s value — the brief transient bright state in the first 0.5 s is excluded, so F0 is the post-transient baseline and true bleaching is slightly faster than shown. Monoexponential fit τ≈131 s (r²=0.989); t75≈37.6 s is EXTRAPOLATED beyond the 26.1 s of real-time data (the same 1.4× extrapolation as before the rescale). Dose-scaled t75 at the 100 mW/mm² reference is ≈17 s, unchanged by the rescale because linear dose-scaling makes the two representations equivalent. APPROXIMATE — 0.5 s-normalized, extrapolated.

review.comment: Maybe we can scale back the curves to make the curves to be that both Voltron2 and ASAP5 are measured under the same illumination intensity

photobleach.note: Cross-GEVI entry from the ASAP7y paper (Hao 2026; primary subject ASAP7y). Digitized (blue ASAP5 curve) from Fig. 2g: normalized fluorescence over 1 min of continuous two-photon imaging of Mi1 neurons in vivo (Drosophila) on an AOD random-access microscope at 940 nm (16 mW post-objective, STAR Methods 'In vivo sensor comparisons in Mi1'; scanned at 1041 Hz), plotted against ASAP7y at 940 nm (green, stays near 1.0). RE-DIGITIZED 2026-09-08 (reviewer flagged the stored curve as 'off'): re-traced at 1 s resolution against the printed ticks (x 0/20/40/60 s at 173/388/604/820 px; y 0.0/0.5/1.0 at 427/276/125 px) and stored at 2 s spacing after a running-minimum pass — this removes the non-physical rise at 25→30 s in the previous array (0.877 → 0.879) and replaces the poor offset-monoexponential (r²=0.975, which forced a flat 0.861 plateau the data never settles on) with a biexponential a=0.101, τ₁=6.98 s, τ₂=1163 s (r²=0.992) that reproduces both the fast first-10-s drop and the continuing slow decline to 0.853 at 60 s. t75 OMITTED: the curve never falls to 75% of F0 within the 60 s window — honest lower bound t75 > 60 s (the fit would put it near 210 s, far outside the data, so it is not stored). 2P power-only measurement: intensityMWmm2 intentionally omitted (no mW/mm² given), NOT dose-scaled to the 100 mW/mm² 1P reference and NOT comparable to the 1P entry above; stands alone. Co-figure GEVI ASAP7y (940 nm) shares this source + Fig. 2g for cross-overlay.

Digitized (blue ASAP5 curve) from the Fig. 3A right sub-panel: F/F0 over 1 min of continuous two-photon imaging of Mi1 neurites in the M10 layer of the medulla in awake Drosophila, 920 nm, 25 mW post-objective, resonant-galvanometric scanning at 354 fps (STAR Methods, 'Two-photon in vivo imaging of Drosophila'); n = 59 ASAP5 neurons from 5 flies. Co-plotted with JEDI-2P (green), which the text describes as having 'slightly better photostability'. Axis calibration from the printed ticks (x 0/20/40/60 s, y 0.0-1.0 in 0.2 steps) and overlay-verified against the source crop. ASAP5 falls to 0.798 at 60 s; biexponential a=0.098, τ₁=3.51 s, τ₂=474 s (r²=0.997). t75 OMITTED: the curve does not reach 75% of F0 inside the 60 s window — honest lower bound t75 > 60 s (the fit alone would put it near 88 s, outside the data, and there is no paper-stated anchor, so it is not extrapolated). 2P power-only: intensityMWmm2 omitted, not dose-scaled, not comparable to the 1P entry. This is the SAME preparation as the ASAP7y-paper Fig. 2g entry above but a different rig/power (Bruker resonant 354 fps at 25 mW vs AOD 1041 Hz at 16 mW), which is why the 60 s endpoint differs (0.80 vs 0.85). Co-figure GEVI JEDI-2P shares this source + Fig. 3A for cross-overlay.

Digitized (blue ASAP5-Kv curve) from the Fig. S4A RIGHT sub-panel — normalized raw traces from long-term (30 min) two-photon recordings of soma-targeted ASAP5-Kv in layer-2 motor cortex of awake behaving mice in vivo, n = 3 mice; 925 nm, 30-160 mW post-objective, LotosScan resonant scanner at 500 fps (STAR Methods, 'Resonant-galvanometric two-photon voltage imaging'). Co-plotted with JEDI-2P-Kv (green); the text calls both 'exceptional' in photostability under two-photon illumination. Axis calibration from the printed ticks (x 0/15/30 min, y 0.0-1.0 in 0.2 steps); the blue line core was isolated by requiring B-R > 90 (which rejects the semi-transparent SEM bands), the largest contiguous run taken per column, then passed through a decreasing isotonic (monotone least-squares) regression before sampling — overlay-verified against the source crop. Time stored in SECONDS. t75 = 970 s (16.2 min) is MODEL-FREE, read by interpolating the digitized points, and lies inside the 1800 s window (extrapolated: false); the biexponential display fit (a=0.116, τ₁=20 s, τ₂=5091 s, r²=0.967) smooths the plateau-then-step structure of the real trace and would place the crossing ~13% earlier at ≈840 s. The Fig. S4A LEFT sub-panel (the 2-min recordings of Fig. 4A, n = 7 ASAP5-Kv / 12 JEDI-2P-Kv) shows the same sensors reaching ≈0.82 at 120 s and is consistent with this curve; only the long-term panel is stored because it is the one that actually crosses 75%. 2P power-only measurement over a power RANGE: intensityMWmm2 intentionally omitted, NOT dose-scaled to the 100 mW/mm² 1P reference and NOT comparable to the 1P entry above; stands alone. Co-figure GEVI JEDI-2P shares this source + Fig. S4A for cross-overlay.
